name: Gamaliel
title: The Wise Pharisee and Teacher of the Law
summary: Gamaliel was a highly respected Pharisee and teacher of the law in the Sanhedrin, known as 'Gamaliel the Elder'. He was the grandson of the famous Rabbi Hillel and was the teacher of the apostle Paul. He is best known for his wise counsel in Acts to let the Christians be, arguing that if the movement was from God, it could not be stopped.

keyEvents.title: Gamaliel's Advice to the Sanhedrin
keyEvents.description: When the apostles were brought before the Sanhedrin, Gamaliel stood up and warned against persecuting them. He argued that if the movement was from humans, it would fail on its own, but if it was from God, they could not stop it.

keyEvents.title: The Apostles Arrested and Brought Before the Council
keyEvents.description: Peter and the other apostles were arrested and brought before the Sanhedrin because they continued to preach about Jesus, which was the background for Gamaliel's intervention.

keyEvents.title: Gamaliel Mentions Theudas' Revolt
keyEvents.description: In his speech to the Sanhedrin, Gamaliel used the example of Theudas, who had gathered followers around him, but the movement fell apart after his death.

keyEvents.title: Gamaliel mentions Judas the Galilean
keyEvents.description: Gamaliel also used the example of Judas the Galilean, who led a revolt during the census, but even his movement was scattered after his downfall.

keyEvents.title: Paul's education under Gamaliel
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul (Saul) stated that he was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel and trained in the law of our fathers with great zeal, which shows Gamaliel's influence as a teacher of the law.

keyEvents.title: The Sanhedrin follows Gamaliel's advice
keyEvents.description: After Gamaliel's wise speech, the Sanhedrin was persuaded. They released the apostles after flogging them and forbade them to speak in Jesus' name, but did not pursue them further at that time.
